about: Prerequisite map for P3 Particle model (brief docs/briefs/2026-11-15-script-four-topics.md, B1, 2026-11-17): every idea the four scripted lessons use, what each depends on (maths included), and where it is taught. Lessons run in syllabus order: p3-particle-model, p3-density, p3-changes-of-state, p3-pressure. P1 Energy comes first, so energy stores, specific heat capacity, internal energy (first meeting) and work done may be recalled. Used when scripting: each script teaches or recalls an idea before it asks about it.

ideas.name: Put numbers into an equation, then rearrange
ideas.taught: KS3 maths; P1 lessons; shown again in each worked example (E67)

ideas.name: 1 kg = 1000 g; 1 kJ = 1000 J
ideas.taught: p1-kinetic-potential, p1-heating; recalled in p3-density key point 2 and p3-changes-of-state key point 3

ideas.name: Volume in cm³ and m³; 1 m³ = 1 000 000 cm³; 1 g/cm³ = 1000 kg/m³
Everything is made of tiny particles (atoms and molecules), always moving
Solid, liquid, gas: arrangement (regular and close, close and random, far apart), movement (vibrate, move past each other, fast random), forces between particles; particle diagrams
Kinetic energy (movement) and potential energy (stored), in joules
ideas.taught: p1-energy-stores; recalled in p3-particle-model key point 2

ideas.name: Temperature is linked to the average kinetic energy of the particles
ideas.taught: p1-heating key point 4 (first meeting); p3-particle-model key point 2

ideas.name: Internal energy: total kinetic and potential energy of all the particles; heating raises it, raising the temperature or changing the state
Melting, freezing, boiling, evaporating, condensing, sublimating; physical and reversible; mass conserved; temperature constant while a pure substance changes state
The particle model is a model: identical solid spheres, not to scale
Mass (kg, g) on a balance; volume (m³, cm³)
ρ = m ÷ V; units kg/m³ or g/cm³; floats if less dense than water (1000 kg/m³)

Required practical 5: regular solid (ruler, V = l × w × h), irregular solid (displacement, eureka can or measuring cylinder: after − before), liquid (measuring cylinder, balance, subtract the empty container); errors and repeats
Gases far less dense than solids and liquids (particles far apart); solids usually a little denser than liquids
Heating and cooling curves: sloping parts change temperature, flat parts change state (latent heat)
Specific heat capacity: energy to raise 1 kg by 1 °C
ideas.taught: p1-heating; contrasted in p3-changes-of-state key point 2

ideas.name: E = m L; specific latent heat of fusion and of vaporisation (J/kg); m is the mass that changes state
Sweating cools by evaporation; steam burns worse than water at 100 °C
Gas particles move in random directions with a range of speeds
Force (N) and area (m²); pressure = force ÷ area, in pascals
Gas pressure: collisions with the walls; force at right angles to the wall
Constant volume: hotter gas, faster particles, more collisions with the walls each second and harder, so higher pressure
Constant temperature, fixed mass: p × V = constant; halve the volume, double the pressure
Doing work on a gas (pushing a piston) raises its internal energy and temperature (bicycle pump)
ideas.taught: p1-power key point 4 (work done); p3-pressure key point 4
